results.evidence: InviteRow adds `isExistingMember = !!memberEmailConflicts[index]`, applies `' errored'` to the email input and renders "This email already belongs to a member of your organization." Conflicts come from `existingMemberEmails` built from `membersLogic.members`.
`existingMemberEmails` does `if (user?.email) { emails.push(user.email) }` from `userLogic`, so the user's own email is flagged like a member's.

Onboarding is covered: `hasExistingMemberEmail ? 'Remove emails that already belong to your organization'` in `continueDisabledReason`. The per-row Submit gets `|| isExistingMember`. But the settings modal's batch submit button isn't shown, so I can't confirm it carries a reason mentioning removing existing members; `canSubmit` going false only disables it.
Client: `email.trim().toLowerCase()` on both the member set and `target_email.trim().toLowerCase()`. Server: `user__email__iexact=email`.

Own-email check works before members load, since `user.email` is added even when `members ?? []` is empty. But the patch adds no explicit `loadMembers` call on modal open or logic mount. Whether `membersLogic` auto-loads on mount isn't shown.

The check is in `OrganizationInviteSerializer.validate_target_email`, which runs during serializer validation before any create. A DRF list serializer validates all rows first, so a member in any position yields a 400 with nothing created. The bulk view isn't shown, so this rests on the standard list-serializer flow.

`raise exceptions.ValidationError("A user with this email address already belongs to the organization.", code="already_member")` inside `validate_target_email`, so it is attributed to the `target_email` field with code `already_member`.

No change touches error-tracking behaviour. The loader `inviteTeamMembers` has no failure handling, and no filtering of already_member rejections was added. The author admits they didn't confirm where the report came from.
There is no `inviteTeamMembersFailure` listener and no `loadMembers` call after a server rejection. The listeners only handle `inviteTeamMembersSuccess` and `addProjectAccess`.

result:
I've added the pre-submit check on the invite row and moved the member check to the backend's validation step. I didn't run any tests, typecheck, formatter, or `kea-typegen`, so none of it is verified.

**Backend** (`posthog/api/organization_invite.py`)
- The "already a member of this organization" check now runs in `validate_target_email`, which covers your own email as well. It matches case-insensitively and returns a 400 with code `already_member`.
- It used to run in `create()`, after earlier rows had already been saved and emailed. Now the whole batch is rejected before anything is created or emailed.
- Ordinary validation errors aren't reported to error tracking. I didn't confirm where the old error tracking report came from, so that part rests on this reasoning.
- I left the old check in `create()` as a guard against a race.

**Frontend** (`inviteLogic.ts`, `InviteModal.tsx`, `OnboardingInviteTeammates.tsx`)
- `inviteLogic` now reads `membersLogic` and `userLogic`. New selectors `existingMemberEmails` and `memberEmailConflicts` flag each row whose email belongs to a member or to you.
- `canSubmit` is false while any row conflicts. The row gets the error styling and the message "This email already belongs to a member of your organization." The per-row Submit button is disabled too.
- The onboarding Continue button shows "Remove emails that already belong to your organization" as its disabled reason. Onboarding and settings share this logic, so both flows pick it up.
- The member list comes from `membersLogic`, so on very large organizations the client-side check may miss someone. The backend check still catches it.
- I hand-edited the kea-typegen type block in `inviteLogic.ts`. Typegen will reconcile it.

**Test** (`posthog/api/test/test_organization_invites.py`)
- The new `test_bulk_invite_with_existing_member_creates_no_invites` sends a bulk request whose last row is the requester's own email in upper case. It asserts a 400 with code `already_member`, no invites created and no mail sent.

The nested ternary I added in `OnboardingInviteTeammates.tsx` probably needs `pnpm --filter=@posthog/frontend fix` to format correctly.
